subject: general
question: How many isotopes of hydrogen element exist in nature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hydrogen has three naturally occurring isotopes: protium (¹H), deuterium (²H), and tritium (³H).
 
• Protium is the most abundant isotope, comprising about 99.98% of hydrogen found in nature.
 
• Deuterium, also known as heavy hydrogen, accounts for about 0.02% of natural hydrogen and is used in heavy water reactors.
 
• Tritium is radioactive and is found in trace amounts in nature, primarily produced by the interaction of cosmic rays with the atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isotopes**

 
 
• Isotopes are variants of a particular chemical element that differ in neutron number, and consequently in nucleon number.
 
• All isotopes of an element have the same number of protons in each atom.
 
 
 
• **Protium (¹H)**
 
 
• Protium has one proton and no neutrons in its nucleus.
 
• It is the most common isotope of hydrogen.
 
 
 
• **Deuterium (²H)**
 
 
• Deuterium has one proton and one neutron in its nucleus.
 
• It is used in nuclear reactors and scientific research.
 
 
 
• **Tritium (³H)**
 
 
• Tritium has one proton and two neutrons in its nucleus.
 
• It is radioactive and has a half-life of about 12.3 years.
 
• Used in thermonuclear weapons and as a tracer in biochemical research.
